speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing sudden-onset vertigo; to determine the cause, I need to ask a few specific questions. First, did this sensation of spinning start immediately, or did it come on gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The symptoms starting while you were going to bed and lasting for approximately 3 minutes strongly suggest a specific inner ear cause. To confirm this, have you noticed any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or tinnitus on the affected side? Also, did the spinning stop completely when you kept your eyes fixed on a single object?

speaker: Doctor
text: The audiometry results are normal, making Meniere's disease unlikely. Have you noticed that the spinning sensation is triggered specifically by changes in your head position, such as rolling over in bed or looking up? Also, have you experienced any recent headaches or double vision?

speaker: Doctor

Given the sudden onset lasting only 3 minutes while in bed, have you noticed any associated neck pain or stiffness?
